title: Approximation of a sheaf supported at closed points
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed
field, $X$ a scheme of finite type over $K$, and $F$ an abelian
sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ whose support is
contained in the set of closed points of $X$. Call a subsheaf
$G\subseteq F$ finitely generated if it is generated by finitely many
sections $s_j\in F(U_j)$ with each $U_j$ an affine scheme and
$U_j\to X$ etale (then $U_j\to X$ is quasi-compact, $X$ being
Noetherian; $U_j\to X$ need not be an affine morphism); equivalently, $G$ is the image of the finite sum
of the corresponding extension-by-zero generators (the construction in
Stacks Project, Tag 03SA). Then $F$ is the filtered colimit of its
finitely generated subsheaves. Every finitely generated subsheaf
$G\subseteq F$ has support a finite set $Z$ of closed points of $X$,
and for $Z$ with its reduced closed subscheme structure and
$i:Z\to X$ the resulting closed immersion one has
$G\cong i_*(G|_Z)$ in the sense of [lem-kun-04ca].
(*Source:* this is the case of Stacks Project, Tag
[0F0N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0N) used in this
chapter, namely the case in which the specialization-closed set $E$ is
the set of closed points of a scheme of finite type over a separably
closed field; the approximating sheaves are then supported on finite sets
of closed points.)

proof.text:
*Step 1 (filtered colimit of finitely generated subsheaves).* Let
$I$ be the set of subsheaves generated by finite families of sections
$s_j\in F(U_j)$ with $U_j$ affine and $U_j\to X$ etale, ordered by inclusion.
The system is filtered, since the sum of two such subsheaves is generated
by the union of their finite families. Every etale $U\to X$ is covered by its affine
open subschemes, each etale over $X$, so a section of $F(U)$ is locally in one of these
finitely generated subsheaves. Therefore the canonical map
$\varinjlim_{G\in I}G\to F$ is an epimorphism of sheaves, and it is a
monomorphism because all transition maps are inclusions; hence it is an
isomorphism.

*Step 2 (the support of a cyclic subsheaf is finite).* Let
$s\in F(U)$ with $U$ affine and $U\to X$ etale, and let $\langle s\rangle\subseteq F$
be the subsheaf generated by $s$. The locus in $U$ where the germ of
$s$ is nonzero is closed: vanishing of a germ is witnessed on an etale
neighbourhood, so its complement is open. If $u$ lies in this support,
then its image $x$ lies in the support of $F$ and is closed. By
[lem-weil-pbc-etale-residue-field-extension-separable], $\kappa(u)$ is
algebraic over $\kappa(x)$. Since $U\to X$ is locally of finite
presentation, $\kappa(u)$ is finitely generated as a $\kappa(x)$-algebra,
so this algebraic field extension is finite. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field]
$\kappa(x)$ is finite over $K$, so $\kappa(u)$ is finite over $K$. Also
$U\to X$ is quasi-compact ($U$ is affine and $X$, of finite type over a
field, is Noetherian, hence quasi-separated), so $U$ is of finite type
over $K$ by [lem-kun-etale-lfp], and $u$ is closed in $U$ by
[lem-kun-closed-point-field] (a) applied to $U$. Thus every point
of the support upstairs is closed in the finite-type $K$-scheme $U$, and
[lem-kun-finite-closed-subscheme] makes that support finite. The
support of $\langle s\rangle$ downstairs is exactly its finite image in
$X$, since the stalk of $\langle s\rangle$ at a geometric point $\bar x$
is the subgroup of $F_{\bar x}$ generated by the germs $s_{\bar u}$ at the
lifts $\bar u$ of $\bar x$ to $U$ (stalks commute with the sheafified image
of $j_{U!}\mathbf Z\to F$, Stacks Tag 03SA), together with the definition of
support [def-kun-support], with geometric-point independence supplied
by [lem-kun-support-geometric-point-independent]. Finally this image
lies in the support of $F$, hence consists of closed points.

*Step 3 (finitely generated subsheaves).* A subsheaf generated by
finitely many sections $s_1,\dots,s_m$ is the sum of the cyclic
subsheaves $\langle s_j\rangle$, so its support is the union of their
supports, which is a finite set $Z$ of closed points by Step 2; in
particular $G$ is supported on $Z$, and therefore $G\cong i_*(G|_Z)$
for the closed immersion $i:Z\to X$ by [lem-kun-04ca].

split_report.summary: Repaired the approximation statement by defining finitely generated subsheaves using finite families of sections on affine etale charts, as required by the Tag 03SA construction. Removed the duplicate residue-field node and rewrote the cyclic-support step to use the existing separable-algebraic residue-field node together with the finite-presentation argument yielding finiteness before taking the finite image in X, and recorded the resulting citations.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the blueprint proof steps: filtered colimit of finitely generated subsheaves; finite support of cyclic and finite-generator subsheaves; and closed-immersion pushforward description.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by R-cpa3048 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Both R-cpa2914 points repaired: finitely generated now uses Tag 03SA generators over quasi-compact charts, Step 2 proves finiteness upstairs in U (closed support, residue fields finite over K via lem-weil-pbc-etale-residue-field-extension-separable + lem-kun-closed-point-field, lem-kun-finite-closed-subscheme) and maps to X; i_*(G|_Z) form via lem-kun-04ca honest for separably closed K; citers lem-kun-0f1f-vanish/-gen use it as written. FIX more, RETURN less: (1) E7/B3 wording: 'U_j->X affine' read as an affine morphism makes the colimit clause false for non-separated X (plane with doubled origin: no etale U->X that is an affine morphism hits a doubled origin, so a skyscraper there is not generated); restated as 'U_j an affine scheme, U_j->X etale (quasi-compact as X is Noetherian)', Step 1 cover = affine opens of U; (2) C1: Step 2 now justifies quasi-compactness of U->X needed by lem-kun-etale-lfp and cites lem-kun-closed-point-field (a) on U for closedness of u; (3) C1: 'stalk formula for extension by zero' replaced by the elementary stalk description of the generated subsheaf with Tag 03SA.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
